rationale: 701.44a is the subrule that actually spells out the explore procedure and its "otherwise" branch: no land card is revealed, so the permanent gets a +1/+1 counter. 104.3c carries the other half, that losing the game comes from being required to draw from an empty library, which revealing never is.

702.16b is the only protection subrule that governs how spells interact with a protected permanent, and it limits that to targeting; Day of Judgment destroys all creatures without targeting, so Goblin Outlander dies. 608.2j gives the Human/Cleric point for Daunting Defender and 702.93a gives undying's return-with-a-counter wording.

701.27a states what transforming does and that any permanent represented by a double-faced card can do it, which is why the Convicted Killer copy transforms too. The second group holds the copy-persistence fact stated three interchangeable ways: a copy doesn't change when the original's copiable values change (707.2b), copying a double-faced permanent uses the face that's up (707.8), and transforming doesn't create a new object (712.18).

702.16b is the subrule that scopes protection's interaction with an opponent's ability to targeting only, so Teysa's non-targeting "destroy that creature" trigger works normally. The equip (702.16d) and damage-prevention (702.16e) subrules answer different questions and would be wrong hits here.

603.7a is the load-bearing rule: a delayed triggered ability won't trigger for an event that happened before the ability was created. 608.2c puts the fight ahead of the delayed trigger in the written order, and the third group covers the fight itself dealing the damage (701.14a) or the lethal-damage state-based action that would normally have killed it later (704.5g).

701.7a states that creating a token is putting it onto the battlefield, which is why an effect that modifies token creation and one that modifies entering the battlefield are modifying the same event. 616.2 states that applying one replacement effect can make another become applicable, which is how Doubling Season gets to apply after Gather Specimens.

701.7a makes creation and entering the battlefield one event, 616.2 lets Crafty Cutpurse's effect become applicable after Gather Specimens is applied, and 614.5 is why Gather Specimens doesn't get a second bite at the modified event.

701.27a is what transforming does and why the Instigator Gang copy can do it, and 701.27e is the rule that a "transforms into [something]" trigger looks at the characteristics right after the transform, so the trigger goes off. The third group states the copy survives the flip, three interchangeable ways (707.2b, 707.8, 712.18).

702.47a states that splice is revealed as you cast the spell and its cost is an additional cost to cast, which is the whole answer. The second group is the casting process saying that announcement and cost payment both happen while casting (601.2, 601.2b, 601.2h), and 608.1 is that the spell only resolves and adds mana afterward.
702.73a is the subrule that says changeling means the object is every creature type, which is the entire basis for Bloodline Pretender being both a Sand and a Warrior.

606.5 (multiple loyalty costs are combined into a single cost) is missing from the chunk set entirely because its line in the CR text is written "606.5 If..." with no period after the number, so the parser's RULE_RE never matches it and the text is dropped rather than folded. 606.4 is the only surviving chunk that covers the cost of a loyalty ability and says that cost may be modified by other effects, so it is the closest retrievable anchor, but it does not state the combining rule and the real fix is the parser.
